findings: OSHelpers implements path/access/media/platform helpers, not root fallback selection; fallback caller still unread. Windows drive/UNC comparison uses win32 normalization/lowercase across hosts, POSIX preserves case. Two original controls confirm lexical behavior, not filesystem equality.

Lexical normalized path does not prove inode or byte identity; Windows case sensitivity options and macOS volume behavior not queried. Extended Windows path parsing and long path utilities are string policies, not native Windows qualification.

isCloudPlaceholder only tests F_OK. Ordinary existing text file returns true (original actual-tempfile control). Function comment requires prior ENOENT read context; caller reachability/precondition enforcement not yet inspected. Not a standalone cloud-state detector.
areDifferentDevices returns false for missing/failed stat rather than unknown. Original tempfile/missing-path control confirms false, which cannot prove same device. No cross-device runtime executed.
checkPathAccessible checks existence and write permission, not read permission/directory type; isDirectory/isSymlink separately return false on errors. TOCTOU snapshot not guaranteed.

tryReadAsDataUri statSync then readFileSync on separate operations; concurrent growth/replacement can bypass size assumption. Reads full file synchronously; extension MIME does not establish decoder support or exact pixel equivalence. Static only.

Resource URL encoding escapes path segments; platform docs in comments are historical assertions, not verified current Obsidian behavior. MIME maps centralize embedding/streaming extension policy but do not test codecs.

Upstream tests simulate process.platform for Windows/WSL cases and use ordinary tempfile for placeholder true. This is not actual Windows/cloud-placeholder coverage. Entire tests read; upstream Vitest not run.

executed_controls.method: Original OSHelpers after Node type stripping; real Node fs/path with desktop Platform stub. Two lexical checks and two actual temporary-file checks. Only created temporary directory removed; no user data touched.

limits: No Windows/WSL/cloud filesystem/native Obsidian or full upstream suite qualification.
